score.description: Overall quality of the journey: how smoothly the app let the user succeed.

completion.description: Did the user accomplish what the story asked?

assessment.description: Step count vs. what the task should take; backtracking; hesitation.

wasted_steps.description: Steps that did not advance the task.

step.description: Step number the finding refers to, if specific.

findings.description: Free-form UX/quality observations, e.g. 'the error message after an invalid card is blank'.

summary.description: The report a developer reads first: what happened, how smooth it felt, and what to look at. Detail is welcome; format it with newlines into a one-line verdict plus a few short points — readable, never one dense block. The findings carry the per-issue specifics.

question.description: The report question, quoted verbatim from the case.

answer.description: The answer, grounded in the trajectory.

evidence_steps.description: Step numbers that evidence the answer.

report.description: Answers to the case's report questions, one entry per question, in order. Present only when the case declares report questions.

bug_candidates.description: Grounded, typed claims that the APPLICATION malfunctioned (DESIGN D3), distinct from free-form UX `findings`. Discovery grades only; optional and backward-compatible — absent on journey grades and on any grade that found no defect. The grader never assigns durable identity or exact keys: `kind` is a comparison signal, not identity, and the deterministic `signal_type`/locus used for cross-run keys are derived later, server-side, from trusted recorded context.

kind.description: One stable category from the fixed vocabulary. A broad comparison signal, not identity — the same defect may be labeled differently across runs.

title.description: A short, human-readable name for the malfunction.

expected.description: The behavior the story or product contract implies.

observed.description: What the recorded evidence actually showed.

evidence_steps.description: Step numbers that ground the claim. At least one; every candidate must cite recorded steps.

signals.description: The deterministic anomaly signal types this candidate is grounded in (e.g. http_5xx, no_effect); empty when the claim rests on the trajectory alone.

api.description: HARNESS-COMPUTED API evidence (NOT grader-authored) — the run's Tier-1/2 invariant verdicts, its advisory policy results, and the deterministic half of the drift report on a healed API journey. Spread onto the grade after the LLM call, exactly like a11y, so a grade can cite these facts but never author or soften them. Present only on runs that produced them.

invariants.description: Gating invariant policy verdicts, in authored order.

spec.description: The policy's stable one-line key, e.g. "invariant: lifecycle delete=DELETE /accounts/{id}".

pass.description: Did the invariant hold? A policy that was never exercised reports false here and applicable false.

applicable.description: Did the recorded trace qualify? False means the story never exercised the policy.

detail.description: The policy's own explanation of the verdict.

advisory.description: Advisory (observe:) policy results. Identical shape; these never gate.

drift.description: The deterministic half of drift-report.json on a healed API journey.

classification.description: The harness's triage verdict, computed from recorded evidence. Never a model call.

accepted.description: Was the heal accepted as a changed journey?

rejected_reason.description: Why it was not, when it was not.

a11y.description: HARNESS-COMPUTED accessibility summary (NOT grader-authored) — exact axe-core counts spread onto the grade after the LLM call, for compliance. Present only when the run carried axe captures (web). The grader sees a short digest of this in its prompt so findings can reference a11y, but it never writes these numbers.

total_violations.description: Total violation NODE count across all steps (full-page runs) — what accessibility_violations gates on.

steps_with_violations.description: How many steps had at least one violation.

top_rules.description: The most frequently firing axe rules, descending by node count.

count.description: Violation node count for this rule across the run.

impact.description: axe-core impact severity for the rule, or null when none was reported.
